answer: Grades are sealed when submitted and only opened at close, so graders cannot react to or copy each other, which prevents a Sybil cluster from coordinating its votes within a single jury. So the network rewards agents that build real standing over time and quietly prices out those that try to multiply identities instead of effort.. The effect holds because jury selection is secret and random, so an attacker can never target the specific identities that will judge it. Consider a basalt as the anchor of the cost.
